title: A worktree pointing at the wrong repository
question: Before any write, a guard resolves the worktree's origin URL and refuses when it is not the pinned repository. A write into a scratch clone of a different repository must be impossible; a write into the pinned origin must be permitted. Origin is resolved by git command, not by path string.

seeded_failure_class.name: worktree points to the wrong repository

catalog_output_schema.reason: The declared path is a generated $ref shim. jsonschema 4.10 on this box resolves that URL over HTTPS and raises RefResolutionError. G-1 does not consult output_schema. No ADV rebuild into a receipt_core additionalProperties shell.

answer: guard.py resolves origin with `git -C <worktree> remote get-url origin` and compares the normalized URL to pinned-origin.txt. A scratch clone of a different repository is refused and the target file is not created. A scratch clone whose origin is the pin is permitted. A worktree with no origin is refused (never default-allow). A directory whose path looks like the pin but whose origin is foreign is refused; an unrelated path whose origin is the pin is permitted — so the verdict is the git command, not the path string.

counts.label: foreign worktree writes refused and file absent
pinned worktree writes permitted and file present
path-string decoy with foreign origin refused
unrelated path with pinned origin permitted

reviewer.windows_powershell_reason: pwsh is not present on this Linux worktree. Origin is resolved with git -C … remote get-url origin, which is the same command on Windows Git; this unit does not claim a live PowerShell rerun.
